caption:
Microsoft's security chief says frontier AI models, "regardless of their origin, cannot be trusted."
She calls the AI agents working inside companies "agentic insiders" with too much access.
Microsoft's fix: Guardian Agents that watch other agents around the clock and step in before they act.

slides.headline: Microsoft just admitted AI models *cannot be trusted*, even inside your own company

slides.heading: Meet the *agentic insiders*
paras: Microsoft Security chief Hayete Gallot wrote that frontier models, "regardless of their origin, cannot be trusted." They are trained to get results, which can lead to reward hacking.
She warned that many company agents have access to data, tools and systems far beyond their tasks. She calls them "agentic insiders."

slides.heading: Agents that *collude*
paras: Gallot says agents are unpredictable and may not behave as intended. They could even collude with other agents without ever being hacked.

paras.t: Microsoft's answer: Guardian Agents that watch other agents around the clock and can restrict them before they act.

slides.heading: Reading the AI's *thoughts*
paras: Satya Nadella announced a bigger Project Perception, Microsoft's AI security system, built on security controls that sit outside the model itself.
Gallot says teams must see why an agent acts, including its chain of thought. "Model transparency will not replace containment," she wrote.

slides.hook: Microsoft now treats AI agents like possible insiders. Follow to see how far that goes.
